questions.question: How long does a full switch with the Current Account Switch Service (CASS) take?
questions.explanation: A full CASS switch takes 7 working days, and you choose the switch date.

questions.question: How much does it cost a customer to use CASS?
options: A fee taken later by your new bank
questions.explanation: CASS is free for customers.

questions.question: What does the Current Account Switch Guarantee promise?
options: Your new bank will pay you a bonus
Interest and charges caused by a failed switch are refunded
questions.explanation: If anything goes wrong with the switch, the Guarantee means interest and charges caused by it are refunded.

questions.question: After a full CASS switch, payments sent to your old account details are…
options: Frozen until you call your old bank
questions.explanation: CASS redirects payments sent to your old details, so nothing gets lost.

questions.question: A “full switch” with CASS means…
options: Your old account closes and everything moves to the new one
You keep both accounts and copy some payments
questions.explanation: In a full switch, payments move across and the old account closes.

questions.question: Why do most bank switch bonuses need a FULL switch, not a partial one?
options: The bonus terms usually say so: the bank wants your whole account
questions.explanation: Switch bonuses usually require a full CASS switch. A partial switch typically won't qualify.

questions.question: A switch offer says “pay in £1,000”. Usually that means…
options: Deposit at least £1,000 within the deadline, often from an external account
questions.explanation: It's a deposit requirement, usually within a time limit. Check whether transfers between your own accounts at that bank count.

questions.question: A switch offer needs 2 active Direct Debits. What does “active” usually mean?
options: Set up, even if not yet collected
At least one payment has actually been collected
questions.explanation: Active usually means at least one payment has gone out. Set Direct Debits up early.

questions.question: Many switch offers exclude you if, in a set period, you've had…
options: A previous switch bonus or account with that same bank
questions.explanation: Eligibility rules often exclude recent customers or previous bonus claimants of the same bank (or bank group).

questions.question: What's a “clawback” in an offer's terms?
options: The bank taking the bonus back if you break the conditions, e.g. closing the account early
questions.explanation: Some offers can reclaim the bonus if you close the account or break the terms within a set period.

questions.question: What is a Direct Debit?
options: A payment you push yourself each time
An instruction letting a company collect payments, which can vary, from your account
questions.explanation: A Direct Debit lets an organisation collect money from your account. The amount can change, but you must be told in advance.

questions.question: Direct Debit vs standing order: what's the key difference?
options: You set and control a standing order; a Direct Debit is collected by the company and can vary
Standing orders are only for businesses
questions.explanation: You control a standing order's amount and dates. A Direct Debit is pulled by the company.

questions.question: The Direct Debit Guarantee means…
options: You get an immediate refund from your bank if a payment is taken in error
Your bank pays your bills if you can't
questions.explanation: If an error is made, your bank must refund you straight away.

questions.question: Since 2020, UK overdrafts are mostly charged as…
questions.explanation: FCA rules banned fixed daily and monthly overdraft fees. Overdrafts are now priced with a simple interest rate.

questions.question: Compared with an arranged overdraft, an unarranged overdraft's rate can be…
questions.explanation: FCA rules stop banks charging more for unarranged overdrafts than arranged ones.

questions.question: A sort code identifies…
questions.explanation: The sort code identifies the bank and branch. The account number identifies your account.

questions.question: Why does a bank check your ID when you open an account?
questions.explanation: Banks must verify who their customers are under anti-money-laundering rules.

questions.question: Your overdraft rate is 39.9% EAR. Roughly what does staying £500 overdrawn for a whole year cost?
questions.explanation: 39.9% of £500 is about £200 a year.

questions.question: What is Confirmation of Payee?
options: A check that the name you enter matches the account you're paying
questions.explanation: It warns you if the name doesn't match the account, which helps stop mistakes and scams.

questions.question: Before switching your only current account for a bonus, what's a sensible safeguard?
options: Open a second account to switch from, so your salary and bills aren't disrupted
Cancel all your Direct Debits first
questions.explanation: Many hunters keep a spare account just for switching, so their main money never moves.

questions.question: When you apply for a new current account, the bank…
options: Often runs a hard search, especially if there's an overdraft, which shows on your file
questions.explanation: Many current account applications involve a hard credit search. Space applications out if you're planning a mortgage.

questions.question: What does a UK sort code identify?
options: The bank and branch your account is held at
questions.explanation: A sort code is 6 digits and identifies the bank and branch holding the account.

questions.question: What is a standing order?
options: A company taking payment when it chooses
A fixed payment you set up to leave your account on set dates
questions.explanation: Standing orders are fixed amounts you control, sent on dates you choose.

questions.question: What is the key difference between a Direct Debit and a standing order?
options: Direct Debits are free, standing orders cost money
With a Direct Debit the company takes what it's owed with advance notice; a standing order sends a fixed amount you set
Direct Debits are only for bills
questions.explanation: Direct Debit gives the company control of the amount with notice; standing orders are fixed and fully under your control.

questions.question: Under the Direct Debit Guarantee, if a company takes the wrong amount you are entitled to:
options: A full and immediate refund from your bank
questions.explanation: The Direct Debit Guarantee means any wrong payment is refunded in full and immediately by your bank.

questions.question: What is an arranged overdraft?
options: An agreed amount you can go overdrawn up to, usually charged interest daily
A type of loan with fixed monthly payments
questions.explanation: An arranged overdraft lets you borrow up to an agreed limit, and interest is charged on what you use.

questions.question: As a general rule, overdrafts are usually:
options: One of the more expensive ways to borrow, with APRs often comparable to or above credit cards
questions.explanation: Overdraft rates are often high, so they should be for short-term gaps, not regular borrowing.

questions.question: Which is a habit that reduces overdraft costs?
options: Using the overdraft as extra income each month
Checking your balance before spending and moving money on payday
questions.explanation: Most overdraft cost comes from drifting into it; checking your balance and topping up quickly keeps interest small.

questions.question: What does Confirmation of Payee do?
options: Checks the name you enter matches the account name before the payment goes
Guarantees you get money back if scammed
Confirms your identity to your employer
questions.explanation: CoP warns you when the name you type doesn't match the receiving account, catching mistyped and fraudulent details.

questions.question: Faster Payments transfers between UK accounts usually arrive:
options: Within a few seconds to a couple of hours
questions.explanation: Faster Payments run 24/7 and typically arrive in seconds, though they can take up to two hours.

questions.question: With a basic bank account you generally get:
options: A place to receive money and pay bills, without an overdraft
questions.explanation: Basic accounts let you receive, pay and withdraw, usually with no overdraft and no credit check.

questions.question: When paying someone abroad, which detail set is typically used for a European transfer?
questions.explanation: International payments use IBAN and BIC/SWIFT rather than a UK sort code.

questions.question: CASS moving your account will transfer:
options: Your balance, direct debits and standing orders, and redirect payments to the new account
questions.explanation: CASS moves the balance and payments, redirects anything sent to the old account, and closes the old account.

questions.question: Can you use CASS if you're overdrawn?
options: Often yes, if your new bank agrees to take on the overdraft
Only if you clear it in full first
questions.explanation: Switching with a negative balance is possible if the new bank accepts the overdraft; some may ask you to reduce it first.

questions.question: If a payment arrives at your old account after a CASS switch, what happens?
options: It is redirected to your new account for as long as needed
It is kept by the old bank
questions.explanation: CASS redirects payments to the old account to your new one, so you don't miss incoming money.

questions.question: Cash bonuses for switching a personal current account are generally:
options: Not treated as taxable income for most people
questions.explanation: HMRC treats most personal current account switching incentives as not taxable, but rules can change so check current guidance.

questions.question: What is CHAPS mainly used for?
options: Large or time-critical payments such as house purchases, usually same-day and sometimes with a fee
questions.explanation: CHAPS guarantees same-day transfer for large amounts, commonly used for property purchases, and some banks charge.

questions.question: When you switch using CASS, your old account:
questions.explanation: CASS closes the old account as part of the switch.

questions.question: Which of these can banks lawfully do?
options: Ask for your full password over the phone
Close an account, with notice, giving a reason unless legally barred
Freeze your account to sell you products
questions.explanation: Banks can close accounts with reasonable notice; they never need your full password or PIN.

questions.question: For a joint account, switching via CASS requires:
questions.explanation: Both account holders must agree to a joint account switch.

questions.question: Some current accounts pay interest on credit balances, but usually:
options: Lower than you could get from a dedicated savings account
Tax free with no ISA needed
questions.explanation: Current account interest is usually modest; dedicated savings or ISAs usually beat it.

questions.question: If you dispute a card payment for goods that never arrived, the first step is:
options: Contact the retailer, then ask your bank about a chargeback or Section 75 if paid by credit card
questions.explanation: Complain to the retailer first; your bank can then consider chargeback, and credit card payments over £100 may get Section 75 protection.

questions.question: A adult current account in the UK normally requires you to be at least:
questions.explanation: Adult current accounts generally start at 16-18; under-16s get child or teen accounts.

questions.question: What is an IBAN?
options: An international bank account number used for cross-border payments
questions.explanation: IBANs identify accounts internationally; UK IBANs start with GB.

questions.question: Going overdrawn regularly without an arrangement can lead to:
options: Refused payments, fees or the bank reducing your options, and can affect future applications
questions.explanation: Unarranged overdrafts can mean refused payments and marks that hurt future applications.

questions.question: Why do banks offer switch bonuses?
options: Current accounts are profitable, so they pay to win customers from rivals
questions.explanation: Banks profit from current accounts through fees, lending and deposits, so paying to acquire you can be worth it.

questions.question: Before switching away from a bank you owe money to, you should:
options: Check how the overdraft or debt is handled, as some debts can block or complicate the switch
Transfer the debt to a friend
questions.explanation: Understand what happens to any overdraft or arranged borrowing before starting the switch.

questions.question: What does 'authorised push payment' (APP) mean?
options: A card payment in a shop
You yourself authorise a transfer to a scammer's account
questions.explanation: APP fraud is when you're tricked into making the transfer yourself, which is why it's harder to reverse.

questions.question: Which is the safest way to check a message really came from your bank?
options: Use the phone number printed on your card or the official app, never the number in the message
Click the link in the message
questions.explanation: Caller ID and sender addresses can be spoofed; always contact your bank through official channels.

questions.question: Your bank calls saying your account is at risk and asks you to move money to a 'safe account'. This is:
options: A scam; banks never ask you to move money to a safe account
Fine if they know your name
questions.explanation: 'Safe account' requests are always fraud. Hang up and call your bank using the number on your card.

questions.question: What's the simplest first defence against overspending from your current account?
options: Setting up a separate bills account and keeping spending money elsewhere
Asking your bank for a limit
questions.explanation: Separating bills money from spending money is a simple, effective way to stop accidental overspend.
